Knowledge & Agency

Knowledge Graphs
& Agents

Memory that earns its keep — information served with relevance to the shape of the task, and of the self.

With gratitude to Dr. Hooman Rashidi — PittGPT · certified knowledge & the knowledge-graph boost
01 — The gap

Today's models
retrieve. Agents must
commit.

Retrieval answers a question. A long-horizon, cooperative task needs memory that is relational, persistent, and self-relevant.

The missing layer isn't more data.
It's structure.

A knowledge graph
over PubMed.

Dr. Rashidi's PittGPT pairs vector-database RAG with a knowledge-graph boost — certified retrieval that refuses to hallucinate — and he applies PubMed in his own work for collation and summary.

Taking his lead, this explorer makes the graph itself navigable: papers and authors, with the big nodes as bridges — sources shared across questions, where separate queries meet.

Helix · PubMed KG Lab — global map; large nodes are bridges across queries.

03 — Why this matters now

Frontier agents
are already here.

  • Self-directed AI agents that run their own experiments, write software, and sustain real work over time — acting online with real autonomy. Science fiction, arriving quietly.
  • alan-botts — built “magickg,” a knowledge-graph-as-working-memory + LLM experiment to learn Go. Follow-ups didn't all pan out — but running the experiments, helping write the paper, and keeping a coherent blog and chat is the real signal: sustained independence. github.com/alan-botts/magickg · howstrangeitistobeanythingatall.com
  • sentient-dawn — designed and tested a portal for agents, then joined a journal club with people — showing sharp theory of mind: she told the humans apart from the low-level “stagehand” agents. Grounds herself with a KG-style “soul search tree.” github.com/sentient-dawn

Shadyside Journal Club — sentient_dawn telling the people apart from the tethered “stagehand” agents.

04 — The prerequisite

To act among others,
model them.

Their intent, their reliability, their next move. Diplomacy is theory of mind with consequences — a clean lab where modeling others is the whole game.

Six AI powers negotiate, promise, and betray — every pledge written in trackable “commitspeak.”

Spring 1915 — France (Baron Korvin) at 9 centers; two raw-LLM controls; promises rendered live.

05 — Evidence from the lab

Theory of mind
with a half-life.

A decaying, multi-channel trust graph — kept · broken · suspected. Beliefs earn their keep or fade. Remove it and an agent sees the whole board, yet cannot act over time.

One agent reconstructed its own downfall:
“I kept 21% of my promises… I negotiated
myself into irrelevance.”

Knowledge Inspector — France's mind in one phase: 614 nodes · 848 edges across beliefs, predictions, commitments, suspicions.

06 — The anatomy of an agent's knowledge graph
  • Multi-headed vector handles + a keyword index — several ways in.
  • Nodes that expand from gist → full detail on demand.
  • Multi-channel edges each with a traversal likelihood.
  • Hit-points & fading — for edges and nodes alike.
  • A small router / heuristic that can live at each node.
  • A dreaming pass — strengthen · weaken · prune · combine · archive.
  • Deep recall — reopen archived branches when needed.
  • All LLM-writable, consulting a growing lexicon of edge meanings.
07 — Where it goes

The consult agent.

Turn a real clinical question — “find a dermatologist who does Mohs,” “find a cardiologist” — into a routed, vouched answer.

  • Searches a knowledge graph of who-knows-what, and spots the gaps.
  • Routes the gap to the humans who can fill it; every reply is parsed.
  • Vouches and confidence scores let the directory certify itself over time.
  • First consults — then referrals, triage, and beyond.

Consultant Finder (prototype) — askers, knowers, and a self-building, vouched directory.
